profile.address: Albert Street, DBT Data - Harrisonburg Center, Harrisonburg, Virginia, 22802
profile.reading:
This Harrisonburg, Virginia property has changed hands several times since it was first built, and its ownership history is itself part of the region's data-center story. The roughly 100,000-to-102,000-square-foot building on a 13-acre parcel near North Main Street was completed in 2007 and marketed early on as a "cyber integration center," a secure facility designed for government and security-sensitive hosting clients. DBT-Data, a Northern Virginia data-center developer, sold the property to defense contractor Harris Corporation in 2010 for roughly $41.6 million; Harris then invested close to $200 million in improvements before deciding to exit the cloud-hosting business altogether. DBT-Data reacquired the facility in 2013 for about $35 million, at which point it was reported to have roughly 7,500 kilowatts of conditioned IT power capacity, Tier III certification from the Uptime Institute (at the time, the only such certification in Virginia or Maryland), and LEED Silver certification for its building systems. DBT-Data stated its intent to operate the site to federal standards, including FISMA compliance, for government and enterprise clients.

That second DBT-Data ownership period was brief. According to the company's own published project history, Harrisonburg is now a past project: DBT-Data sold the facility in September 2014, for roughly $59 million, to an entity connected to the private-equity firm GI Partners. Subsequent public reporting on financing tied to the building places its current ownership with AC DataCom Digital Infrastructure Investments, a firm founded in 2022 with ties to Carter Validus and Iroquois Capital Advisors; a 2023 financing filing described the roughly 100,000-square-foot facility, designed for up to 40 megawatts of capacity, as having been fully leased to health insurer Anthem since 2015.

In short, the building most closely associated with DBT Data in Harrisonburg has not been owned or operated by DBT-Data for more than a decade. DBT-Data's current business, per its own project listings, centers on developing data-center land in Northern Virginia and central Ohio rather than operating completed facilities directly, consistent with a company that presents itself as a real-estate investment and development firm for data-center sites rather than a long-term operator. A reader researching this address today is more likely encountering an Anthem-leased facility under different ownership than an active DBT-Data operation, and the building's several changes of hands since 2007 illustrate how quickly ownership of even a large, purpose-built data center can turn over in a competitive market like Northern and Central Virginia.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. This Harrisonburg campus, lacking a published megawatt figure, cannot be ranked among Virginia's disclosed capacity and therefore does not factor into assessments of the state's AI infrastructure readiness.

Without specifications, this site cannot be evaluated for relevance to AI scaling. To matter to grid constraints or compute availability, DBT Data would need to publish the power capacity, IT load density, and power delivery timeline for this facility.
